title: A Time-Frequency Framework for GKP Codes
abstract: We develop a time--frequency framework for lattice GKP codes in which ideal codewords are realized in the modulation space $M^\infty$ and identified, through a vector-valued Zak transform, with a finite logical fibre over the continuous syndrome torus. Multi-window Gabor analysis then represents the logical vector by a finite block of adjoint-lattice coefficients. We prove that the normalized block map is an isometry, obtain an explicit recovering projection, and derive stable logical reconstruction. We further construct normalizable GKP approximants as lattice-envelope Gabor multipliers and establish weak-$*$ convergence and asymptotically isometric encoding. Finally, we recover displacement syndromes from phase relations between translated coefficient blocks and quantify their stability under additive perturbations.
summary: This paper develops a time-frequency framework using Gabor analysis to analyze lattice GKP codes. It proves that the logical information can be uniquely and stably recovered from a finite block of phase-space coefficients. Furthermore, it provides a method to extract the continuous displacement syndrome by analyzing the phase relationships between these coefficients, offering a theoretical blueprint for syndrome measurement.
main_problem: To develop a rigorous time-frequency framework for lattice Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes, specifically addressing how to stably reconstruct the finite logical information from localized phase-space coefficients.
main_result: The authors prove that the normalized block map is an isometry, establishing a unique and stable determination of the logical vector from sampled coefficients, and derive a stable estimator for the continuous displacement syndrome from phase relations between coefficient blocks.
method: The work employs the vector-valued Zak transform and multi-window Gabor analysis to map ideal codewords to finite blocks of adjoint-lattice coefficients, allowing for reconstruction theorems and syndrome estimation.
model_or_system: The system is based on lattice GKP codes, which encode quantum information into highly structured states within the infinite-dimensional Hilbert space of oscillators, analyzed using modulation spaces and Gabor frames.
key_observables: The finite block of adjoint-lattice Gabor coefficients, and the phase relations between translated coefficient blocks used to estimate the displacement syndrome.
important_parameters: The lattice structure ($\Lambda_D$), the regularization parameter ($\epsilon$), and the noise level ($\eta$) governing stability bounds.
main_assumptions: The analysis is conditional on access to the complex amplitudes (coefficients) and relies on asymptotic convergence and weak-* approximations for finite-energy states.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the Zak transform framework, then developing the adjoint-lattice coefficient model and proving the isometry, followed by deriving the block-correlation estimator for syndrome extraction, and finally quantifying the convergence of this estimator for finite-energy states.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful mathematical tool for understanding continuous variable quantum error correction, linking abstract phase-space representations (Gabor analysis) directly to measurable syndrome information in a stable, quantifiable manner.
